## Summary

Verbatim (zh):

> 各位要用要么马上就用，要么不用，别犹犹豫豫，不然炮灰就是你。
>
> https://kyc-helper.org/zh/，一个 AI 驱动的 KYC 身份文件生成器。它用 AI 生成逼真的护照、驾照、身份证和账单等合成文档，号称支持 20 多个国家。

Translation: "If you're going to use it, either use it right now or don't at all — don't hesitate, or you'll be the cannon fodder. https://kyc-helper.org/zh/ — an AI-driven KYC identity-document generator. It uses AI to generate realistic synthetic passports, driver's licenses, ID cards, and utility bills, claiming support for 20+ countries."

What it is: an open promotion, in a large Chinese-language expat channel on X, of a commercial SaaS whose stated purpose is defeating KYC (Know Your Customer) identity verification with AI-generated fake documents. The "use it now or you're cannon fodder" framing is classic gray-market urgency bait — implying a closing window before detection, enforcement, or the tool's operators get shut down.

## Why it matters

- **Fraud-ecosystem intelligence, not a to-do.** Deliberately captured as reference with no Inbox task: using a service that forges passports/licenses/IDs/bills to pass KYC is identity-document fraud — criminal in essentially every jurisdiction, including the UAE. The vault records that this class of tool is now marketed brazenly on main with six-figure view counts; it does not operationalize it.
- **Relevant context for the user's own KYC surface:** synthetic-document SaaS at this scale is one of the forces driving banks/exchanges to tighten document checks, push liveness/biometric verification, and freeze accounts with any document anomaly. Awareness of the attack tooling explains part of the friction on the legitimate side.
- **Marketing template worth recognizing:** "马上用，要么不用" (act now or abstain) + 炮灰 (cannon fodder) is the standard pump template for gray-market tools with a short expected shelf life — the seller monetizes the window before enforcement catches up, and late adopters absorb the risk. Same shape as expired-play promos in trading channels.
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) every capability claim is the vendor's own — the poster himself hedges with 号称 ("it claims"); zero verification the output passes real KYC. (2) Unverified service of this type is at least as likely to be a scam, honeypot, or malware drop targeting would-be fraudsters as a working product. (3) Engagement (1.2k likes / 340k views) may be inflated; reply count (51) is modest relative to views. (4) Services like this have short lifespans — the domain's future content was not probed and is not archived.
